title: Tile types, substrate assessment and waterproofing boundary
audience: Tilers who assess substrates and decide where tiling depends on a waterproofing system
learningOutcomes: Identify common tile types and their fixing requirements.
Assess a substrate for movement, flatness, moisture and suitability for the tile.
Identify the waterproofing boundary and refer wet-area work where the position is not established.

instruction.heading: Tile types need different fixing
instruction.body: Ceramic and porcelain tiles differ in water absorption, weight and size, and porcelain is often denser and harder to cut. Natural stone is porous and can stain, and some stones need sealing. Glass and mosaic tiles need a fixing and a grout suited to their size and their backing. Large-format tiles need flatter substrates and a suitable adhesive. Check the manufacturer data for the tile and the adhesive, and record the product.

instruction.heading: Assess the substrate and the boundary
instruction.body: Refer wet-area waterproofing to a competent or licensed person, and do not tile over a membrane that you cannot identify.

procedure: Identify the tile type and its manufacturer data, and record the product.
Assess the substrate for flatness, movement, moisture and bonding.
Check whether the area is a wet area or needs a waterproofing system.
Refer any waterproofing or wet-area work, and do not tile over a membrane you cannot identify.
Record the substrate assessment and the referral.
Confirm the adhesive and the substrate preparation with the manufacturer data before fixing.

workedExamples.situation: A client wants large-format porcelain tiles laid over a timber floor that feels bouncy when walked on.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the porcelain be laid on the timber as it is?
workedExamples.reasoning: Not as it is. The bouncy floor indicates movement, and large-format tiles need a stable and flat base. Refer the floor for assessment and strengthening, record the finding, and do not tile until the substrate is confirmed suitable.

equipmentAndPpe: Moisture meter where trained to use it
Manufacturer data for tile and adhesive

commonErrors.error: Laying large tiles on a bouncy timber floor.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer and strengthen the base, and confirm it before tiling.

commonErrors.error: Tiling a wet area over a membrane that you cannot identify.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer the waterproofing and confirm the membrane before tiling.

commonErrors.error: Using a tile adhesive not suited to the tile type or the substrate.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the manufacturer data for the tile and the adhesive.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Treat wet-area waterproofing as work for referral to a competent or licensed person.

Tiling licence positions. New South Wales: a contractor licence is needed for tiling work where labour and materials, GST included, exceed $5,000 (NSW Government page, last updated 23 June 2026). Queensland: wall and floor tiling is a QBCC licence class (class page last reviewed 31 August 2021). The $3,300 figure on that page limits incidental work outside the class; it is not a tiling threshold. Victoria: a tiling-only job needs no registration, but combining tiling with another trade on one job does (Consumer Victoria page, last updated 9 July 2025). South Australia: anyone carrying on business as a building work contractor needs a licence; the CBS guide gives no dollar threshold and does not name tiling (no date shown).
Completing this lesson does not give a tiling, waterproofing or building licence, certificate or authority.

qualityStandard: The tile type and adhesive are checked against the manufacturer data and recorded.
The substrate is confirmed flat, stable, dry and bonded before tiling.
Wet-area waterproofing is referred and not assumed.
documentationEvidence: Substrate assessment record with flatness, movement and moisture findings
Product record for tile and adhesive
Referral note for any waterproofing or wet-area work
summary: Match the fixing and the adhesive to the tile type and the substrate.
Assess the substrate for flatness, movement, moisture and bonding before tiling.
Refer waterproofing and wet-area work, because the position is not established.

knowledgeChecks.question: Large porcelain tiles are to be laid on a timber floor that feels bouncy. What is correct?
options: Lay them as they are on the floor now without any changes at all
Refer and strengthen the base, and confirm it is suitable before tiling
Use more adhesive to hold the tiles down firmly on the bouncy floor
Lay them with wider joints between the tiles and the edges of the room

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the status of the waterproofing position in this course?
options: Confirmed as not required in any state or territory at all in Australia by any authority
Confirmed as covered by a tiling licence in every state and territory of the whole country
Named in Queensland's QBCC classes, but not established for other states, so it is referred until checked
Confirmed as covered by a handyman licence held by the worker on the job site in every state

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say about natural stone tiles?
options: It is porous and can stain, and some stones need sealing
It is always denser than porcelain
It needs no check of the manufacturer data
